acceptanceCriteria: Fixture provider with one supplied gap, one status, one case link: build admits all three; `import_parity` counts them; `docs_gaps --id p:flow:a` returns the supplied gap marked `supplied`; the case link suppresses `missing-manual-cases`.
5,000 observations in a `/2` manifest build successfully.
Supplied gaps/status never raise trust (remain `generated` / attributed).
body: GitHub beamfall/corvint#1244 (filed 2026-10-19 against build main-fa8afe6). `corvint-corpus-adoption-provider/1` admits subjects, claims, relations, journeys, observations and a fixed set of typed details (`claim_kind`, `flow`, `paragraph`, `test_link`, `coverage`, `ticket`, `intent_comparison`). Several common documentation-corpus families have no typed home and are lost at export:  1. Producer-supplied gaps. `Artifact.Gaps` is compiler-computed only; `ProviderRecord` has no gaps field, so curated gap ledgers (with kind, reason, owner disposition) cannot be imported. 2. Readiness / proof status per subject (e.g. `blocked`, `ready`, `proven` with a reason and the evidence ids it rests on). There is no status detail; forcing it into untyped claims makes it unqueryable by `docs_gaps`/`docs_coverage`. 3. Manual test case <-> subject links. Legacy cases are searched from a separate export file outside the corpus; there is no relation type or detail joining a case id to a flow/endpoint subject, so `docs_gaps` cannot use them (`missing-manual-cases` is driven only by journeys). 4. Test-run receipts beyond the test-validity document format, and observations are capped at 4,096 per corpus even for `/2` manifests.
title: Adoption providers: typed supplied gaps, status detail, manual-case links, /2 observation bound (GitHub #1244)
